items.original_sentence:
Abstract
​This repository contains the primary dataset and forensic reconstruction of a Universal Metric Invariant (13.7g) that functioned as the "Hard-Coded" standard for Bronze Age trade between the Indus Valley Civilization and the Levant.
items.suggested_treatment: Reframe the universal 13.7g trade standard as a hypothesis explored by this notebook, not an established archaeological fact.
items.evidence_required: Independently dated weight catalogs from both regions, mass distributions, chronologies and evidence of transmission.

items.original_sentence:
Forensic Case Study: The Eshtemoa Silver Hoard
​The Eshtemoa Hoard (Judean Highlands) contains five jugs filled with over 26kg of "Hacksilber" (cut silver).
items.suggested_treatment: Attribute the five-jug/over-26kg claim to a verified excavation inventory or label these numbers unverified.
items.evidence_required: Primary excavation publication, findspot inventory, vessel counts, original units and aggregate mass.

items.original_sentence:
​The 13.7g Calibration: When the data is re-calculated using the Indus 13.7g Standard, the "scraps" resolve into perfect fractions:
​6.85g (The Beqa/Half-Unit)
​3.42g (The Quarter-Unit)
​The Conclusion: The silver was physically "hacked" to satisfy the requirements of a Registry that demanded the 13.7g Indus standard.
items.suggested_treatment: Separate 13.7/2 = 6.85 and 13.7/4 = 3.425 arithmetic from the unsupported claim that silver was deliberately cut to these values.
items.evidence_required: Individual measured fragment masses, precision, competing weight bases, null model and rounding rationale for displayed 3.42g.

items.original_sentence: The Result: When you use the 13.7g weight to calibrate the water flow, the clock perfectly predicts when the Moon will disappear and reappear.
items.suggested_treatment: Reframe the claimed perfect lunar prediction as a proposed experiment, not a demonstrated result.
items.evidence_required: Clock geometry, flow rate, timing calibration, lunar ephemeris, dates, error bars and held-out predictions.

items.original_sentence: * The Calibration: If you take a 13.7g chert weight to the top of the High Island salt dome, the "Metric Friction" changes slightly compared to sea level.
items.suggested_treatment: Frame salt-dome balance differences as a testable physical hypothesis, not demonstrated ancient calibration.
items.evidence_required: Quantified gravity difference, instrument sensitivity, controls, and historical evidence; distinguish mass from weight.

items.original_sentence: In the Registry, these are the "Grounding Pins." A 13.7g silver jar buried in a salt dome doesn't just sit there; it is protected from electromagnetic "noise," preserving the Metric Purity of the metal for thousands of years.
items.suggested_treatment: Qualify or remove the salt-dome shielding and millennia-long metric-purity preservation claim pending physical evidence.
items.evidence_required: Proposed shielding mechanism, corrosion chemistry, measurable preservation endpoint, environmental controls and independent source.
